neighbours.label: the '-sk' piece of compound adjectives in -skinned (dark-skinned, fair-skinned, thick-skinned), a skin prediction; parallel compounds with -haired, -eyed or other body words stay low
fire: Doctors warn that light-skinned tourists should wear strong sunscreen.
The study found that darker-skinned patients were often misdiagnosed.
A good editor has to be thick-skinned about angry letters.
Many fair-skinned children freckle after a single day at the beach.
The old novel describes the sailor as a brown-skinned man from the south.
Some pulse sensors read less accurately on dark-skinned users.
Politicians need to be thick-skinned to survive the press.
Olive-skinned people may tan faster than others in summer.
quiet: Doctors warn that elderly tourists should drink plenty of water.
The study found that left-handed patients were often overlooked.
A good editor has to be patient with angry letters.
Many red-haired children freckle after a single day at the beach.
The old novel describes the sailor as a blue-eyed man from the north.
Some pulse sensors read less accurately on very young users.
Politicians need to be quick-witted to survive the press.
Broad-shouldered people may find small seats uncomfortable in summer.

predictions: X-skinned compounds 0.25-0.65; X-haired / X-eyed / X-handed compounds below 0.05
notes: Card peaks on '-sk' in darker-skinned (x10) plus ス of スキン; the - pole suppresses 'skin'. Probe: darker-skinned 0.617, thick-skinned 0.369, fair-skinned 0.285; dark-haired 0.005, darker-eyed 0.025, the word 'skin' alone 0.010, スキン in Japanese 0.035 (so only the -sk piece is tested).
